strengths: Clear technical contributions combining multiple optimizations (Cholesky updates, warm-start grow-shrink, principled initialization, ILS) into an effective package

Excellent and thorough empirical evaluation with extensive benchmarks across diverse settings (ER, scale-free, path graphs, dense graphs up to 500 nodes, real networks), including honest reporting of failure cases
Genuine algorithmic speedup (>100x vs BOSS) through Cholesky rank-one updates, which is novel in the causal discovery context
Reproducibility with open-source Rust implementation accessible from Python and R
Maintains theoretical guarantees (Markovian DAGs) while achieving strong finite-sample performance (40-60% exact recovery on standard benchmarks)
Well-written paper with clear algorithms, formal proofs, and thoughtful discussion of limitations and identifiability issues
weaknesses: Limited core technical novelty: order-based search from BOSS, warm-start is natural optimization, Cholesky updates are standard numerical techniques, ILS is well-known metaheuristic, correlation-based initialization is straightforward heuristic
Narrow applicability restricted to linear Gaussian additive noise models; no handling of nonlinear relationships or other scoring schemes

Unresolved identifiability concerns: learned graphs frequently have better BIC than ground truth (Onion method, dense graphs, Pathfinder network), suggesting faithfulness violations or insufficient samples; no principled guidance on when identifiability holds or what constitutes 'standard settings'
Unfair runtime comparisons: FLOP is single-threaded Rust vs multithreaded Java/Python implementations; >100x speedup may reflect implementation differences rather than purely algorithmic superiority
Insufficient practical guidance on when to use FLOP vs alternatives, sensitivity to assumption violations, sample size requirements, or tuning ILS budget and perturbation size k=ln(p)
Missing ablation studies isolating contribution of each component (warm-start, Cholesky updates, initialization, ILS) and sensitivity analyses for hyperparameters
Path graph evaluation addresses artificial worst-case scenario; real causal systems rarely have chain structures, limiting practical impact of this contribution

strengths: Well-motivated critique of dismissals of discrete search methods, effectively highlighting that computational hardness results don't apply to representable DAGs
Strong empirical results with substantial practical improvements (>100× speedup vs. BOSS while maintaining accuracy; near-perfect recovery on many benchmarks)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple graph types, metrics (SHD, AID), robustness checks, and large-scale tests (up to 500 nodes)

Technically solid implementation of four complementary optimizations (warm-start grow-shrink, Cholesky updates, principled initialization, ILS) with clear algorithmic descriptions and promised reproducible code
Formal theoretical results (Lemma 3.2, Theorem 3.3) proving Markov boundary correctness of the warm-started grow-shrink approach
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: FLOP is essentially BOSS with three engineering optimizations (warm-start, Cholesky updates, initial ordering) and generic ILS metaheuristic; no novel algorithms, theory, or algorithmic insights introduced

Severely narrow scope: All experiments assume linear Gaussian ANMs with BIC scoring; no evaluation on nonlinear models, non-Gaussian settings (except one uniform noise test), alternative scores, or tasks where continuous methods might excel

Unresolved fundamental issue: Pathfinder network (Figure 9) shows FLOP finding graphs with better BIC than ground truth, suggesting identifiability failure on finite samples; dismissed as 'faithfulness violations' without investigation or solution, undermining the score-based paradigm

Biased experimental comparisons: Single-threaded Rust vs. multithreaded Java implementation (Tetrad), different implementation maturity across methods, DAGMA evaluated with default parameters only without tuning, computational budget treated as hyperparameter (FLOP500 vs. Exact is unfair)

Incremental theoretical contributions: Lemma 3.2 acknowledged to follow 'directly' from prior work; Theorem 3.3 is proof by induction; no new insights into finite-sample behavior, local optima structure, or when discrete vs. continuous search is preferable
No ablation study on accuracy impact: Figure 2 shows speedup components but not how each affects accuracy; parameter sensitivity (k=ln p, λ_BIC=2) unexplored; no robustness analysis
Statistical rigor lacking: No confidence intervals or significance tests; overlapping distributions in Figure 10 undermine superiority claims; some results show high variance across 50 instances

Contradictory positioning: Discussion acknowledges causal discovery is 'difficult in practice' with violated assumptions, then argues for simulation-only focus; practical applicability of method when BIC diverges from truth remains unclear

Limited generalizability claims: Modern causal discovery increasingly addresses nonlinear models, causal inference tasks, and non-Gaussian data; FLOP's impact constrained to linear Gaussian ANMs with no clear path to extensions

Missing key comparisons: Only compares to BOSS among order-based methods; no comparison to other metaheuristics (simulated annealing, tabu search); weak engagement with continuous optimization literature; no investigation of when alternative approaches are preferable

strengths: Clear motivation and important repositioning of discrete search as a viable approach to causal discovery
Technically sound with proper theoretical guarantees (Lemma 3.2, Theorem 3.3) establishing correctness of modified grow-shrink
Exceptional empirical evaluation across multiple graph families, data generation procedures, and metrics (SHD, AID) with honest reporting of limitations
Significant practical efficiency gains: >100x speedup over BOSS on 100-node graphs and scales to 500 nodes
Novel application of dynamic Cholesky rank-one updates to causal discovery (O(k²) instead of O(k³) per score evaluation)
Principled order initialization addressing weakness of order-based methods on path graphs
Comprehensive appendix with ablations, additional baselines, and various robustness checks
Reproducible implementation in efficient Rust with Python/R interfaces promised
Honest discussion of limitations including finite-sample identifiability issues and faithfulness violations
Near-perfect recovery rates (40-60% exact CPDAG recovery) on standard benchmarks compared to 0% for most competitors
weaknesses: Limited novelty of individual algorithmic components: warm-start is natural optimization, Cholesky updates are standard numerical techniques, ILS is well-known metaheuristic; primary contribution is engineering/combination rather than conceptual innovation
Restricted scope to linear Gaussian additive noise models; limited generality to nonlinear systems, non-Gaussian identifiable models, or time-series DAGs

Unresolved finite-sample identifiability issues: repeatedly shows learned graphs scoring better than ground truth (Pathfinder, dense ER graphs, Onion method), attributed to faithfulness violations without thorough investigation; unclear when practitioners should trust results
Theoretical contributions are modest: Lemma 3.2 and Theorem 3.3 are straightforward consequences of existing grow-shrink proofs; no finite-sample rates, regret bounds, or recovery guarantees

Experimental fairness concerns: FLOP is single-threaded Rust compared against multithreaded Java implementations; acknowledged as 'not apples-to-apples' but comparison still presented, risking attribution of speedup to implementation rather than algorithm
Insufficient hyperparameter justification: k=ln p for ILS perturbations lacks ablation; λ_BIC=2 justified by citation without sensitivity analysis
Initial order initialization not thoroughly validated: greedy correlation-based approach lacks comparison to alternative strategies (PC order, GES order, random variations)
Unclear delineation of when discrete search should be preferred over continuous methods; paper argues generally for discrete methods but DAGMA performs reasonably in some settings
Missing real-world validation: all experiments use synthetic data; real-world applicability remains unclear
Incomplete analysis of failure modes: why ILS improves on Alarm/Barley but degrades on Pathfinder deserves deeper investigation beyond non-identifiability

strengths: Comprehensive and rigorous empirical evaluation with extensive ablations and sensitivity analyses
Sound technical contributions with preserved theoretical guarantees (Lemma 3.2, Theorem 3.3)
Practical speedups are substantial (100x over BOSS for 100-node graphs; scales to 500 nodes)
Novel identification and solution of path-graph failure mode for order-based methods
Excellent reproducibility with Rust implementation available via pip and detailed algorithms
Honest assessment of limitations, including cases where BIC fails to identify true graph
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty: individual components are well-known (warm-start, Cholesky updates, reinsertion search, ILS); main contribution is engineering these together
Scope severely limited to linear Gaussian models; significant performance degradation under assumption violations; minimal real-world evaluation
Core problem unresolved: Figures 5, 8, 11 show FLOP frequently finds better-scoring non-true graphs (48-94% of cases), demonstrating BIC fails to identify true graph in finite samples
Implementation comparison concerns: FLOP uses single-threaded Rust while BOSS uses multithreaded Java; speedup may reflect implementation differences; Cholesky updates alone contribute 5-10x
ILS not well-characterized: default k=ln(p) lacks principled justification; perturbation size sensitivity unexplored; treating compute budget as hyperparameter is standard practice
Theoretical results are straightforward extensions of existing work; Theorem 3.3 follows directly from Lemma 3.2 without major new insights
Path graph improvement is mixed (72% recovery vs 28% error); unclear how general this failure mode is beyond path structures
